trickyParts: Identity is read INSIDE launchShimmedProcess's per-issue serialize lane, not after it: the in-memory issue->window map (`issueWindows`, formerly `issueWindowIds`) now stores the opened pane's full locator (window id + pane id + pid + start ticks). `recordedLocatorsInWindow` includes that entry, so a concurrent second spawn on the same issue (queued behind the first launch) can verify the first pane by identity and split into its window; with the plan's original 'read identity after the lane' shape the existing test 'serializes two concurrent first spawns on the same issue into a single new window' opened two windows because the first launch's claim was not yet persisted when the second probed.

Test 'ensureController gracefully stops, never kills, a controller locator whose pane id was reissued...' asserts the shutdown reached the controller socket, no kill-pane, fresh `new-window controller`.

CI red at 0a4dc25f (run 34718138952, `test` job): two `LEGION_E2E=1`-gated tests in real-shutdown-e2e.test.ts failed -- `kills a real pane wrapping a real worker-shim after its stop timeout...` and `lets a root's own self-report POST to /process/exit resolve...` -- both on `expect(await waitForPaneGone(paneId)).toBe(false)` (pane still alive). Root cause: that file seeds worker/root locators by hand from a REAL tmux pane without `panePid`/`paneStartTicks`; under the new contract an identity-less locator never verifies, so `stopProcess` treated the pane as already gone (log: `not killing pane %1 ... no recorded process identity`) and never killed it. Classification: a pre-existing fixture in a file I had not touched that needs rule (a) -- and a verification gap on my side: CI sets LEGION_E2E=1 and LEGION_TMUX_LIVE=1 and I had only run the latter locally. Added one real-tmux negative control in the same file: the same live pane recorded with start ticks off by one is never killed (no `kill-pane`), its claim clears, the tree closes, the pane survives; the daemon log carries both identities. Proof: `LEGION_E2E=1 LEGION_TMUX_LIVE=1 bun test real-shutdown-e2e.test.ts` 4/4 green 5x in a row (and 5x more after a type tightening), 4/4 while processes+api and processes+index suites ran concurrently, and the whole daemon package under the exact CI env 898 pass / 0 fail / 0 skip with two other suites running alongside.

Review round (CHANGES_REQUESTED 5188293250), both blocking findings from a legacy no-identity verdict being read as not-our-process where our own live process is what is there. B1 (r3997829564): `rewriteIssueWindowId` repointed live legacy locators (workers on resurrect; the root on spawn_worker) to the fresh window, so their real window fell out of `knownWindows` and the sweep kill-windowed it. Fix per architect direction (reviewer option a): a locator's `tmuxWindowId` is never rewritten; `probedWindowId` now iterates `recordedLocators(issue)` (root locator if root, each worker claim's locator, the in-memory `issueWindows` entry, in that preference order) and returns the first window whose pane verifies, else `undefined` (dropping the stale in-memory entry); `launchShimmedProcess` records a fresh window in `issueWindows` alone; `rewriteIssueWindowId`/`recordedWindowId`/`recordedLocatorsInWindow` deleted. Regression tests: `legacyLiveTreeFixture` (live, identity-less root %0 in @42 [+ implementer %3], fake list-windows reporting @42/@43 owned with activity 0) drives both repros: probe->resurrect->reconcileTmuxWindows(0) and spawnWorker(tester)->spawnWorker(planner)->reconcile; assert the legacy locators keep `@42`, the fresh worker lands in `@43`, the next worker splits into `@43`, and no kill-window/kill-pane at all. The pre-existing test pinning the rewrite was rewritten to the new contract (stale claims keep their dead window; later workers split into the fresh one). B2 (r3997829566): `closeTreeLocked` derived `skipGraceful` from `probe()`, which reports a legacy locator dead without touching tmux, so a live legacy root was never sent `shutdown`. Fix: `closeTreeLocked` takes the `verifyPaneProcess` verdict itself and passes `skipGraceful` only for `pane-gone`; regression test asserts the shutdown frame reaches `/state/workers/architect.sock`, no kill-pane, tree closed, locator cleared. Non-blocking (r3997829569): `samePaneIdentity(current, stopped)` (pane id + panePid + paneStartTicks) replaces the pane-id-only comparisons in `markWorkerDeadLocked`, `retireUnconfirmedBoot`, and closeTree's delete guard (which now snapshots the stopped locator by value). Fast-follow items all landed: `tmux.panePid(server, paneId)` lost its window-id `rows[0]` branch and doc sentence (tmux.test.ts:30 deleted); both docs/solutions notes rewritten to the pane-id-only probe with the removed `firstPaneId`/`windowAlive` named only as history; triple logging collapsed to one line per decision -- `resurrectDeadTree` guards silently via `verifyPaneProcess` and hands its verdict to `removeTreeWindow` -> `stopProcess({ refused })`, `controllerAlive` passes `{ refused: verdict }`, and `stopProcess`'s gate logs only a refusal it decided itself (a verified verdict is never accepted as `refused`; the pane is always re-verified at kill time) -- verified with a throwaway counting identity lines: root probe->resurrect 1, closeTree 1 per pane, controller 1; the undiscriminating watchdog test (`paneProcessVerified: () => false` cannot tell reissued from gone) deleted, acceptance 7 stays on the ProcessManager-level test; `/%1/` in the tree-close gate test became `/%1[^\n]*pid 777/`; the `Errors row 3` comments now describe the behaviour. AGENTS.md worker bullet: a later worker splits into a recorded window only while some recorded pane in it verifies, else a fresh window; a locator's tmuxWindowId is never rewritten. Daemon package under LEGION_E2E=1 LEGION_TMUX_LIVE=1: 900 pass / 0 fail.

Re-home onto main (architect decision A after main landed LEGION-21's Runtime boundary, #962, and GitHub reported #981 CONFLICTING so no CI ran for bb80ca31). The design is unchanged; only its home moved from ProcessManager into TmuxRuntime (runtime-tmux.ts), and the branch's code commits were squashed into one. Interface delta on runtime.ts: TmuxLocator gains panePid/paneStartTicks; ProbeResult's dead arm is a REQUIRED discriminant `{status:'dead', reason:'gone'} | {status:'dead', reason:'not-recorded-process', detail}` (kubernetes/FakeRuntime return honest `gone`; FakeRuntime.occupyHandle drives `not-recorded-process`); Runtime.stop gains `refuseKill` so a caller whose own probe already decided (and logged) passes the verdict down instead of the runtime re-verifying and re-logging; `sameProcess` for tmux compares paneId+panePid+paneStartTicks. Inside TmuxRuntime: identity is read in `spawnIssueProcess`'s per-issue serialize lane (split and fresh-window paths) and in `spawnController`; `recordedPaneIdentity` throws when /proc/<pid>/stat is unreadable right after tmux reports the pane (launch failure through the caller's existing path); `verifyPaneProcess` (pid -> start ticks -> OMP) is the one chokepoint gating `probe`, `stop`'s kill-pane, and `probedWindowId`; `issueWindows: Map<IssueKey, TmuxLocator>` replaces `issueWindowIds` and is one more candidate for `probedWindowId`, which picks the first recorded window whose pane verifies and never rewrites a locator's window id (B1); `deps.persist` and the pane-id backfill are gone (`issueLocators` is read-only). ProcessManager stays tmux-free (runtime.contract.test.ts's vocabulary gates still pass): `probeTree` returns the full verdict and logs `treating <tree>'s root as dead: <detail>` once at the decision point; `closeTreeLocked` passes skipGraceful only for `gone` and refuseKill for `not-recorded-process` (B2); `resurrectDeadTree` probes silently and hands the verdict to `removeTreeProcess`; `controllerAlive` logs once, stops with refuseKill, then clears. State v25 with a pure-bump `migrateV24State` (fields optional: a legacy locator never gets an identity, it probes dead and is resurrected onto a recorded one). Tests: identity tests moved to runtime.contract.test.ts against the FakeTmuxServer (per-pane startTicks, `procStat(pid)`, `reissuePane`), with contract rows for both dead reasons run across FakeRuntime and TmuxRuntime; ProcessManager-level B2/resurrect/controller/watchdog cases run against FakeRuntime with the discriminant; the pre-rebase tmux-integration tests in processes.test.ts were re-applied (fixture population sweep) and kept as end-to-end pins (kill-pane absence, --resume, both-identities logs); the real-tmux e2e negative control (start ticks off by one -> no kill, pane survives) and the LEGION_TMUX_LIVE real-/proc test are kept. The `kill -0` existence check inside isOmpPane is unchanged from main (redundant after the stat read; left in place to keep the change scoped).

Review round 2 (CHANGES_REQUESTED 5188762941 at cfe6d066). B3 (r3998125105): `tmux.panePid` folded every nonzero `list-panes` exit into 'pane gone', so a runner-timeout-killed tmux client or `server not responding` made `verifyPaneProcess` say `gone` -- `probe` would report a live root dead (a second copy resurrected beside it) and `stop` would skip the graceful ask and clear the locator over a live pane. Fix at the tmux layer: `lookupPane(server, paneId)` returns `{status:'present',pid}|{status:'absent'}|{status:'failed',detail}` -- `absent` only when stderr matches `PANE_GONE_STDERR` (moved from processes.ts into tmux.ts and exported; the same contract the kill-pane path applies), an unparseable pid is `failed`. `PaneVerdict` gains `{verified:false, reason:'listing-failed', detail}`; `TmuxRuntime.probe` THROWS `Error(describePaneVerdict)` ('cannot verify pane %N: <argv> exited 1: <stderr>') rather than answering alive or gone; `TmuxRuntime.stop` order is graceful ask -> `if (refuseKill) return` -> verify -> verified: kill-pane (PANE_GONE_STDERR tolerated) / listing-failed: `throw new ProcessStopFailed(locator, detail)` / other: return without killing. `probedWindowId` simply does not reuse a window whose panes cannot be verified. Every probe caller handles the throw: `probeLocator(locator, subject)` (extracted; used by probeTree/controllerAlive/resurrectDeadTree) rethrows so the resync `onProbe` logs and retries; `closeTreeLocked` probes inside the same try as its stop so a listing failure surfaces as StopFailed (tree stays `lingering`, locator untouched, 502 to the API); `retireUnconfirmedRoot` catches a probe failure, logs, and re-arms the registration deadline; the boot watchdog's `probeAlive` logs 'liveness probe did not complete; re-arming' and returns true. `isProcessGoneError` (ENOENT/ESRCH) narrows the `/proc` reads in `readPaneStartTicks` and `isOmpPane`; the redundant `kill -0` in `isOmpPane` is gone.

B4 (r3998125111): the 'missing a pane id' throw in `verifyPaneProcess` is deleted -- a locator without a pane id is the identity-less (`no-identity`) case: the graceful ask is still sent over its socket, the kill is refused, and the locator clears as if gone. Non-blocking threads: r3998125116 `removeTreeProcess` stops first and clears the locator in a `finally` guarded by `tree.locator === locator` (a failed stop no longer leaves a cleared locator behind a live pane); r3998125119 `readPaneStartTicks` catches only ENOENT/ESRCH; r3998125122 the legion-state comment says what a missing identity means at runtime (never verifies, resurrected on first probe) instead of 'backfillable'; r3998125124 `recordedLocators` dedupes the `issueWindows` entry by reference. `drainSpawns` also awaits `this.resurrecting.values()` so a test that drains spawns also drains a resurrection that a spawn's probe started.

Fixture rule (tests): a fake `list-panes` that means 'pane gone' must say so on stderr -- `paneGone()` = `{stdout:'', stderr:"can't find pane", exitCode:1}` swept over 33 processes.test.ts fakes and the three live-tmux fixtures (which now return stdout/stderr/exitCode separately); a bare exit 1 is a listing failure the runtime refuses to act on, and the two new ProcessManager B3 tests plus the runtime-contract listing-failed tests drive exactly that. Vocabulary gate list in runtime.contract.test.ts extended with `lookupPane`/`PANE_GONE_STDERR`. Identity-detail pins are `expect.stringMatching` over both identities plus the `/proc` stat/cmdline read counts, never log wording.

Flake remediation (Sami's rule: a pre-existing flake I hit comes with a fix). Tick-bounded `windowCount` waits in processes.test.ts (`flushEventLoopUntil` against real fs I/O) became `windowCounter().reached(n)` (a promise settled by the fake `run` on the n-th new-window) plus `await processes.drainSpawns()`. The dispose test pins `workerBootRegistrationDeadlineIntervals: 1_000` for the same reason.

Rebase onto main after #973 (idle-retire), #983 (pin bump), #980 (launch hold, per-claim reconnect isolation, workspace clone) -- AGENTS.md conflicts resolved twice keeping main's new bullets beside mine. #980 fixture interactions under the identity contract: `skipEnablePromotion` -> `skipEnableLaunches` (2 sites); #980's reconnect-isolation test gets `...paneIdentity()` + `livePanes`; its held-recoveries test uses `paneGone()`; my watchdog test dropped its `{ skipEnableLaunches: true }` (its spawn must launch); index.test.ts's launch-hold test needed a `list-panes -> %1 4242` fake AND `readProcessCmdline: async () => 'omp\0'` (no real process behind the fake pid, so without the cmdline fake the root's pane failed the OMP step and the worker opened a second window instead of splitting -- the test's `['new-window','split-window']` pin is exactly the window-reuse-by-identity contract).
